points.description: A constructor is called automatically whenever an object is created, whereas a function must be called explicitly.
points.partial_credit: 2 marks if only says constructor is special/used to initialize objects without stating automatic vs explicit calling, or the idea is vague or has a minor error

points.description: Constructors have no return type, whereas functions must declare a return type.
points.partial_credit: 0.5 if says only that functions return values without stating constructors have no return type

rubric.notes: Full marks need the core difference: a constructor runs automatically when an object is created, while a function must be called explicitly. Any wording is fine. The return-type difference is worth the last mark; give part marks for vague or half-stated ideas, and no marks for unrelated descriptions or wrong claims (e.g. constructors return values).
